subsystems.name: Impeller and hub
subsystems.role: the rotating blade set that moves the air.
parts: sometimes a ring joining the blade tips

subsystems.name: Motor
subsystems.role: a brushless DC motor spins the impeller at a controlled speed.

subsystems.name: Bearings
subsystems.role: let the shaft spin quietly for years.

subsystems.name: Frame and mounting
subsystems.role: holds the motor and seals against the case or radiator.

subsystems.name: Control and connection
subsystems.role: sets speed and reports it back.

buildSteps.title: Design the blade
buildSteps.detail: Curvature, blade count and tip clearance are tuned in fluid simulation and wind-tunnel tests for either high airflow or high static pressure.

buildSteps.title: Mould the impeller and frame
buildSteps.detail: Glass-fibre-reinforced thermoplastic is injected into polished steel moulds; blades and hub come out as one balanced piece.

buildSteps.title: Wind the stator
buildSteps.detail: Copper wire is wound around laminated steel poles, then the assembly is potted and fitted with the control circuit board.

buildSteps.title: Build the rotor
buildSteps.detail: Permanent magnet segments are bonded into a steel cup that presses onto the shaft.

buildSteps.title: Fit the bearings
buildSteps.detail: The bearing (sleeve, ball or fluid-dynamic) is pressed into the hub so the shaft turns with minimal play.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and balance
buildSteps.detail: Rotor, stator, frame and cable come together, then each unit is spun and balanced to cut vibration and noise.

buildSteps.title: Test and rate
buildSteps.detail: Fans are run to measure speed in rpm, airflow in cubic metres per hour, static pressure in millimetres of water and sound level in dB(A).

prerequisites.why: small, cheap and long-lived, with electronic speed control instead of brushes to wear out.
they set the torque and efficiency of the motor.
blades need to be thin, stiff and accurately shaped at low cost.
bearing quality decides noise and service life.

prerequisites.tech: Motherboard PWM fan headers and control software
prerequisites.why: they let the system vary fan speed with temperature instead of running flat out.

pathway.milestone: standard 120 mm and 140 mm PWM fans on cases, coolers and radiators
pathway.unlocks: quiet, automatic airflow control tuned to component temperatures.

pathway.milestone: higher static-pressure designs and daisy-chained fans sharing one cable
pathway.unlocks: more airflow through dense radiators and filters with less wiring clutter.

pathway.milestone: better bearings and blade shapes with sound under 20 dB(A) at moderate speed
case-level airflow sensing and control integrated with system software
pathway.unlocks: fans that spin only as fast as the installed components actually need.
